newsitem.title: USA: Ameritech refiles for Mich. long distance.
newsitem.headline: Ameritech refiles for Mich. long distance.

text.p: Ameritech Corp said Wednesday it refiled an application with the Federal Communications Commission to provide long distance telephone service in Michigan.

Under the Telecommunications Act of 1996, the regional Bell companies can enter the lucrative long distance market when they comply with a checklist confirming their local markets are open to competition.
Ameritech said the FCC is required to make a decision on the application within 90 days.
Michigan regulators in February ruled that the company met the checklist, but Ameritech said it withdrew its first application when questions arose over its interconnection agreement with AT&T Corp.

The new filing is more than 10,000 pages, with another 5,000 pages on a web site, Ameritech said. The company said it believes it has met all of the legal and regulatory requirements for entry into the Michigan long distance market.
Ameritech has estimated the long-distance market in its five-state region at $9 billion.
